title: Finite-Cadence Refresh Equilibria for Streaming Prior-Anchored Ridge: A Closed-Form Forgetting Window and Spectral Correction
abstract: arXiv:2611.14586v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recursive estimators on drifting streams must forget stale data fast enough to track the target, yet slowly enough to average out noise. In prior-anchored ridge regression, this trade-off admits a closed-form spectral decomposition in which each eigen-direction interpolates between the data solution and the prior with pull weight $s_i = \rho / (\mu_i + \rho)$. When the anchor is refreshed every $k$ steps, we show that the moving-frame offset converges to a finite-cadence equilibrium that lags the pure-leaky path by an explicit $\Delta_k(s)$ while reducing estimation variance by a factor $\Psi(s, r_k)$. Minimizing the cycle-averaged risk gives $\omega^* = (4\nu^2 \Sigma / c')^{1/3}$, $c' = \sigma^2 d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\rho)$, and the plug-in strength $\rho^* = \sigma^2 / (n\delta^2)$. A random-matrix deterministic equivalent extends both laws to finite dimension, renormalizing the anchor to $\rho_{\mathrm{eff}} = \rho (e^{\zeta q} - 1) / (

translated_title: 漂移流上先验锚定岭回归的有限节律刷新均衡：闭式遗忘窗口与谱校正
translated_abstract: 漂移数据流上的递归估计器必须足够快地遗忘陈旧数据以跟踪目标，同时又必须足够慢地遗忘以平均掉噪声。在先验锚定的岭回归中，这一权衡存在闭式谱分解，其中每个特征方向以拉动权重 $s_i = \rho / (\mu_i + \rho)$ 在数据解与先验之间进行插值。当锚点每 $k$ 步刷新一次时，我们证明动框架偏移收敛于一个有限节律均衡，该均衡以显式的 $\Delta_k(s)$ 滞后于纯泄漏路径，同时以因子 $\Psi(s, r_k)$ 降低估计方差。最小化周期平均风险给出 $\omega^* = (4\nu^2 \Sigma / c')^{1/3}$，其中 $c' = \sigma^2 d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\rho)$，以及插入式先验强度 $\rho^* = \sigma^2 / (n\delta^2)$。随机矩阵确定性等价方法将上述两条规律推广到有限维情形，并把锚点重归一化为 $\rho_{\mathrm{eff}} = \rho (e^{\zeta q} - 1) / ($……
tldr: 该论文为流式先验锚定岭回归建立了闭式理论：证明周期性刷新锚点收敛到有限节律均衡，给出显式的遗忘窗口与谱校正，并推导出最优刷新节律 $\omega^*$ 和最优先验强度 $\rho^*$ 的闭式规律，且通过随机矩阵确定性等价推广到有限维情形。
en_tdlr: The paper derives a closed-form theory for streaming prior-anchored ridge regression, showing that periodically refreshed anchors converge to finite-cadence equilibria with an explicit forgetting window and spectral correction, and obtains closed-form optimal refresh cadence and anchor strength extended to finite dimensions via random-matrix deterministic equivalents.
